newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks mostly off at midday, but techs firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks mostly off at midday, but techs firmer.

text.p: U.S. stocks were mostly weaker in quiet pre-Thanksgiving midday trading, but drew some support from a revitalized technology sector.

"The techs are resuming leadership after a couple days' break. But the Dow itself is taking a well-needed pause," said James Cramer, president of Cramer Co. "I do give thanks to the Dow for not going up and up and up. Every time it cools off, the rally becomes more sustainable."
The Dow industrials lost 30 to 6498. Dow tech component IBM rose 3/4 to 158-3/4.
The tech-studded Nasdaq composite rose two to 1283 as heavyweights Intel rose 2-1/4 to 126, Cisco rose 1/8 to 67-3/8 and Microsoft rose 1-1/4 to 155.
The S&P 500 lost one to 755. Losers outpaced gainers 11-10 on active NYSE volume of 194 million shares.
"There's not much to crow about. The market is giving back some of its gains," said Alan Ackerman of Fahnestock & Co.
Analysts said the bulk of the day's activity likely took place in the first hour of trading after a battery of economic reports. The long bond was up 2/32 to yield 6.43 percent, off earlier highs.

Bonds initially extended gains on news that third-quarter Gross Domestic Product growth was revised to 2.0 percent against an expected 1.7 percent growth rate. Also reported was weekly jobless claims, unchanged at 342,000 and higher than the forecast 336,000 for the November 23 week.
Later, bonds pulled off highs after October durable goods rose 0.1 percent against an expected 2.0 percent drop.
The Chicagoland Business Barometer rose to a seasonally adjusted 57.6 in November against an expected 55.1 reading.
The bond market trade association backs an early close of 1400 EST/1900 GMT today but stocks will hold a full session.
U.S. financial markets will be closed Thursday for the holiday. Stocks will hold an abbreviated session Friday, with regular session activity ending at 1300 EST/1800 GMT.

Oil stocks were another focus Wednesday and were generally weaker amid profit-taking. Texaco lost two to 98-7/8, Exxon was off 1-3/8 to 93-1/2, Chevron fell 1-1/4 to 66-7/8 and Mobil slipped 1/2 to 120-7/8.

NYMEX crude was firmer, with the January futures contract up 17 cents to $23.79 a barrel. OPEC ministers started their winter conference on Wednesday in Vienna looking to set production levels for at least the first half of 1997.
They are widely expected to roll over their current 25.03 million barrels per day ceiling.
Meanwhile, analysts were impressed by the market's rally in November as the Dow has risen some 500 points. "We had Christmas in November," said Ackerman, a market strategist.

But some thought the January effect, the tendency for small caps in January to outperform larger companies, may not take place. They noted individual investors have recently been pouring money into blue chip stock funds. "A lot of the money is earmarked. It's from foreigners who want to be in Intel and IBM" and not more speculative small caps, Cramer added.
Among individual issues, America Online added 2-3/4 to 35-3/8. Cowen upgraded AOL to buy from neutral.
Texas Instruments extended gains, up two to 63. Salomon upgraded the stock to strong buy from hold.
Walt Disney lost 2-1/4 to 74, giving back Tuesday's gains made on its strong quarterly earnings report. Dean Witter downgraded the stock.
Forrester Research, which provides products and services that gauge how technology affects business, surged 5-3/4 to 21-3/4 in its first day of trading.
-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730
